'''Jandai''' is an [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] of the [[Quandamooka people]] who live around the [[Moreton Bay]] region of [[Queensland]].<ref name="AIATSIS" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite book |title=Minjerribah Moorgumpin Elder-in Council Jandai Language Dictionary |publisher=Minjerribah Moorgumpin Elder-in Council Aboriginal Corporation |year=2011 |isbn=9780987096609 |location=Dunwich, Queensland, Australia}}</ref> Other names and spellings are Coobenpil; Djandai; Djendewal; Dsandai; Goenpul; Janday; Jendairwal; Jundai; Koenpel; Noogoon; Tchandi.<ref name=":SLQ">{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/20?embed=true|title=Jandai|author(s)=[[State Library of Queensland]]|accessdate=17 May 2022}}</ref><ref name=":SLQ2">{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/63?embed=true|title=Goenpul|author(s)=[[State Library of Queensland]]|accessdate=20 May 2022}}</ref> Traditionally spoken by members of the [[Goenpul|Goenpul people]], it has close affinities with [[Nunukul language]] (spoken by the [[Nunukul|Nunukul people]]) and [[Gowar language]] (spoken by the [[Ngugi people]]).<ref name="AIATSIS" /> Today now only few members still speak it.

== Classification ==
The three tribes that comprise the Quandamooka people spoke dialects of a [[Durubalic languages|Durubalic]] language.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Dixon |first=R. M. W. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MSqIBNJtG0AC&pg=PR34 |title=Australian Languages: Their Nature and Development |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |year=2002 |isbn=978-0-521-47378-1 |volume=1 |author-link=Robert M. W. Dixon}}</ref> The language that the Goenpul tribe of central and southern Stradbroke Island speaks is Jandai, and the [[Nunukul language|Nunukul dialect]] of northern Stradbroke island was called Moondjan, the term for its distinctive word for "no".<ref name=":SLQ2" />

Bowern (2011) lists five [[Durubalic languages]]:<ref>Bowern, Claire. 2011. "[http://anggarrgoon.wordpress.com/2011/12/23/how-many-languages-were-spoken-in-australia/ How Many Languages Were Spoken in Australia?]", ''Anggarrgoon: Australian languages on the web'', 23 December 2011 ([http://pamanyungan.sites.yale.edu/master-list-australian-languages-v12 corrected] 6 February 2012)</ref>

* Jandai (Janday)
* [[Turrbal language|Turrubal]] (Turubul) and Yagara (Jagara)
* [[Nunukul language|Nunukul]] (Nunungal, Moonjan)
* [[Gowar language|Gowar]] (Guwar)

Dixon (2002) considers all but Guwar to be different dialects of the [[Yagara language|Yagara]] language.<ref name=":0" />

== Vocabulary ==
Some words from the Jandai language include:<ref name=":SLQ" /><ref name=":SLQ2" />

* ''Maroomba bigi/maroomba biggee'': good day
* ''Juwanbinl'': bird
* ''Buneen'': echidna
* ''Gagarr'': fish
* ''Murri'': kangaroo
* ''Dumbirrbi'': koala
* ''Gabul'': snake
* ''Bingil'': grass
* ''Humpi'': home/camp
* ''Djara'': land
* ''Juhrram'': rain
* ''Bigi'': sun
* ''Dabbil'': water
* ''Bargan'': boomerang
* ''Goondool'': canoe
* ''Jahlo'': fire
* ''Marra'': hand
* ''Jalwang'': knife
* ''Tabbil'': water
* ''Wanya'': where?
* ''Ragi'' bush
